question: Under the recorded ordinary count with short knots retiring, release, and the recorded taking rule with take-the-oldest (take-the-newest as its swap), on a start whose second pattern's start knot is fixed and of whose members a stated number are left usable: is the set of courses from the first pattern only, over every numbering of the start, disjoint between two second patterns; does the first difference involve a knot of the second pattern's descent; and does one value the law uses at one birth already separate the two, or is the difference composed over several births?
inputs: The starts, the numberings by orbits, the bars, the laws, the takes, the bounds and the guard's limits named in the pre-registration and its data files; this study's definitions and claim; the frozen definitions of the copier study's first ticket for the made designs and descent; the definitions of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001 and the shared definitions of RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001; the engine of PARTS-MEET-AGAIN-20261124-001A, unchanged, read-only.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; for the engine's author, the drafter's scratch prototype and anything it produced beyond what the pre-registration and its data files disclose; any change to a frozen engine; any rule added so that a pattern reads; any numbering left out after its outcome is seen.
primary_observable: For every registered start, number of usable members, take, knot law and numbering: the course from the first pattern only in its canonical form, the meeting round, the knots that link the two patterns with their class, and the knot test of every knot; for every pair of second patterns: whether the two sets of courses over every numbering share a course, on the longest prefix of rounds every run reached; the attribution of the first differing used value (a knot of the second pattern's descent; a third part; round-wide; unclassified); and the verdict handed in one value, composed over several births, or no difference.
comparators_or_controls: No taking rule, where one course over the class is expected; a planted case whose first difference must be classed as a third part (a start knot); a case listed birth by birth by hand; hand-written records for each attribution answer; the made designs of five and six members on the registered numbering; the swap of the treatment; take-the-newest as the swap of take-the-oldest.
resource_budget: About twenty-five minutes in all on at most 6 processes, each under a memory cap; bounds by counts (4 rounds, a stop after the first round leaving more than 800 knots, and the guard's limits as written in the pre-registration).
first_executable_signal: The gate: the hand-listed case reproduced birth by birth, the attribution records classed as registered, the negative control giving one course, and the planted case classed as registered.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' entry; arguments (S1 to S5), checks of the code and reported readings are marked as such. A pair is disjoint only if no course is shared over every numbering on the common prefix; a cell with a run stopped by the guard before round 2 is undecided.
stop_rule: Stop when every registered run is done, every pair of every cell has its three verdicts or is reported undecided with the count, and every prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of two small starts built by hand, to four rounds. 'Which pattern' here is how many members a bar placed by hand left usable. The expected result is that the law hands a count over through a start knot, which is not a pattern reading anything; where one value separates two second patterns the law did it. The rule still uses names: any result is 'under take-the-oldest, whatever the numbering'. It would not show a fold of emergence: the property that the first pattern then makes a pattern of its own is not tested. No claim about living things, minds, physics or time.
